title: r3's ODN-10 justification is false as written: balance.json does NOT load with jint_strict — the top-level balance loader uses jint, which silently truncates a decimal, so a fractional cap does not fail-fast
evidence: spec:130-131: '`balance.json` loads with `parse_integers = true` + `jint_strict`, `core/catalog.odin:675` — a fractional cap would fail-fast at catalog load):**' · catalog.odin:675: 'v, e := json.parse(src.balance, parse_integers = true)' · catalog.odin:680: 'b.logic_hz = jint(obj, "logic_hz", 0)' (all 24 top-level balance keys use jint; jint_strict only at :794-795, the placement block) · catalog.odin:1026-1033: 'jint :: proc(o: json.Object, key: string, def: i32) -> i32 { if v, ok := o[key]; ok { #partial switch x in v { case json.Integer: return i32(x) case json.Float: return i32(x)' (silent truncation) · catalog.odin:1036-1038: '// jint_strict — like jint but a json.Float (a decimal in the file) is a // fail-fast rejection (ok=false), never a silent truncation — the 3.1 // integer-only bar for the NEW catalogs (ODN-5; the old loaders keep jint).'
detail: False claim on five canon surfaces. A minion following the neighboring jint pattern gets 0.5→0 (accrue 0, no terminal pickable, all director spawns silently dead) — the exact ODN-5 fail-fast violation the canon says is impossible.
recommended_fix: Pin the accessor: 'load cap_fraction_permille with jint_strict (the placement precedent, catalog.odin:794) + a 1..1000 range check — the top-level balance loader's jint silently truncates decimals.'
